# 💸 Session Cost Pill — DeepSeek Harness
**Live session spend, right in the composer dock.**

DeepSeek tells you how many tokens you burned. It does not tell you what that cost.
This plugin does
— live, per session, without a single line of patched harness source.
## What you get
The composer dock already tracks turns, speed, tokens, and context. The cost pill joins that row:
| Pill | Shows |

| ⏱ activity | turns · steps · decode speed |
| 💾 usage | total tokens · cache-hit rate |
| **💸 cost

** | **estimated spend for this session** |
| 🪫 context | context-window pressure |
The glyph climbs with the session total, so the row reads at a glance before the number does:
| under $1 | under $5 | under $20 | under $100 | $100 and up |
**Click it** and the breakdown opens: uncached input, cache reads, and output, each priced separatel

y, plus how much
of the total was charged at peak rates and how many steps that covered. It closes o

n Escape, on a click outside, or on
a second click — the browser's own popover behaviour, so the plu

gin ships no dialog state, listeners, or positioning
code of its own.

## Why the number is right
Most cost trackers multiply a session's tokens by one flat rate. That is wrong for DeepSeek twice ov
t cost trackers multiply a session's tokens by one flat rate. That is wrong for DeepSeek twice over.
### 1. DeepSeek has peak pricing
Prices **double** during peak hours, so a single rate per model cannot price a session.
| Model | Tier | Cache hit input | Cache miss input | Output |

| `deepseek-flash` | off-peak | 0.003 | 0.15 | 0.60 |
| `deepseek-flash` | peak | 0.006 | 0.30 | 1.2

0 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | off-peak | 0.022 | 0.66 | 1.98 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | peak | 0.044 | 1.32

epseek-v4-pro` | off-peak | 0.022 | 0.66 | 1.98 |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` | peak | 0.044 | 1.32 | 3.96 |
*USD per 1M tokens, transcribed from Models & Pricing.*
Peak is **01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday–Friday**. Everything else — all weekend — is off-p
is **01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday–Friday**. Everything else — all weekend — is off-peak.
So this plugin prices **every assistant step at the rate in effect for that step's own timestamp**.

A session that
crosses a peak boundary gets a correctly blended total instead of a guess.
### 2. Cache hits dominate, and they are ~50× cheaper
A cache hit costs a fraction of a cache miss. A tracker that folds all prompt tokens into one bucket

will miss the mark
badly on a long agent session — exactly the kind that reads 96% cache-hit.
### Verified against real billing
DeepSeek publishes no pricing API, but its Platform console reports authoritative cost. Checking thi

s plugin's table
against one real account's October `deepseek-flash` usage:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A **0.11% match**. The table is right, and that month's usage was effectively all off-peak — assumin

g peak would have
doubled the estimate.
## How it works

It is an ordinary Cordis client plugin. Nothing in the harness is
patched, forked, or monkey-patched

patched, forked, or monkey-patched.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The pill reads the chat snapshot through the session standard kit and folds it:

- `useChat` → every settled assistant step, each carrying its own `time` and provider `usage`
- `use
Projection('modelSelection')` → the session's model
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`isPeak` classifies one request from its UTC weekday and hour, so pricing is per-request rather than
sifies one request from its UTC weekday and hour, so pricing is per-request rather than per-session.
## Known limits
Honest ones, not footnotes:
- **Chinese public holidays are off-peak in full, and this is not modelled.** That needs a PRC holid

ay calendar, so
weekday windows falling inside a holiday week are priced as peak — slightly overstat

ing those days.
- **The model is priced at session level.** Chat assistant nodes carry `time` and `u

sage` but not the
model, so a session that switched models mid-way prices every step at the most rec

ently used model's rates.
- **Account-level spend is not shown.** DeepSeek's Platform console does e

xpose real billed cost through private
endpoints that authenticate with `x-dsh-auth-token` (not `Aut

horization: Bearer`), and DSH already
holds that grant via `getPlatformSession()`. It is deferred he

re because the browser half of a Remote needs
generated zod codecs.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Types without a build step.** `client.js` ships as plain JavaScript on purpose: the harness inject

s plugin
bundles into the page as a **classic script** (`<script src>`, no `type="module"`), so the

file reaches
the JS engine verbatim. There is no build step and no runtime type stripping on the bro

es
the JS engine verbatim. There is no build step and no runtime type stripping on the browser side.
Types therefore live in **JSDoc annotations**, verified by `tsc --checkJs`. Real, CI-visible checkin

g with no
toolchain. `test.ts` is different — Node strips its types natively.
The suite pins the behaviour that matters:

- peak windows, both edges, the mid-day gap, and weekends
- published rates for both models, off-pea

k and peak
- **one off-peak plus one peak step in a single session**, asserting the summed per-step

rates — the case a
session-wide total provably cannot produce
- an unpriced model renders no pill ra
ther than a wrong number
